Final Fantasy IV

Cecil Harvey

A two-job punisher: Dark Knight on the ground, Paladin in the air

Fastest BRV 15F (Valiant Blow)Fastest HP 13F (Shadow Bringer)Dash 81 (Dark KnightATK 109DEF 1111-hit HP NoHP links Yes

Standing in the meta

Tier C 27th of 30 — 2017 tournament tier list from dissidia.wiki (half matchup values, half expert player votes).

Ranked 27th, in tier C, on the 2017 tier list, which matches the overview: Cecil is commonly placed in bottom / low tier competitively, owing to the constraints of his job system and an unfavourable risk/reward ratio.

Overview

Cecil Harvey fights at close and mid range with two distinct jobs: Dark Knight, built around ground combat and wall rushes, and Paladin, built around aerial combat with a more balanced moveset. Practically two characters in one, he changes job at will — but that change goes through specific HP attacks, a double-edged sword: decent in neutral and as punishes, they are mostly telegraphed and carry long recoveries. Cecil therefore adapts to many situations, at the cost of risk every time he wants to reach a particular job.

Cecil is built neither for pure offence nor for iron defence: he excels as a punisher. Many of his moves have good reach, vertical or lateral, and he punishes the opponent's whiffs effectively with either job depending on the matchup. He has several solo combo routes, which he can set up with an assist depending on whether he is after damage or EX.

His difficulties: below-average frame data (long startups and animations, late cancel windows) that makes filling the assist gauge on whiff dangerous — a fundamental weakness in competitive play, which exposes him to whiff punishes as well as assist punishes. His capricious tracking makes punishing dodges awkward, or even simply hitting a mobile opponent, and his slow or low-priority projectiles limit his zoning.

Competitively, Cecil is generally ranked bottom / low tier. His job system constrains him as few other characters are constrained: good pokes on the ground but no solid aerial poke, with no way to force ground combat to compensate. A ground or air specialist depending on the job, he is judged the strongest in neither register and often takes high risks for a lesser reward. He can nonetheless capitalise on clean hits with an assist when the chance arises.

Strengths

  • Good poking and explosive damage as Dark Knight.
  • Good EX generation as Paladin.
  • Whiff punishment: several moves suited to punishing missed attacks from various angles, such as Valiant Blow, Shadow Bringer and Sacred Cross.
  • Solo combos with heavy bravery damage, able to link into HP attacks.

Weaknesses

  • No safe aerial poke: more vulnerable to whiff punishment on average, and filling the assist gauge is difficult and risky.
  • Situational solo combo starters, which limit the chances to make use of his combo routes.
  • Mediocre zoning: telegraphed projectiles with a good reward on hit but hard to place in neutral.
  • Changing job generally requires telegraphed attacks that expose him to punishes.
  • The job dilemma: specialising in one job always imposes notable compromises, and he cannot rely on a single job on large stages.

Slash 23FMelee Low

A two-hit Paladin bravery attack, valuable for its reward: 20 base, 90 EX, and above all cancels into an attack or a dash on hit — extremely rare outside dash feints and EX Revenge. It opens the most practical Paladin combos on the ground (Radiant Wings, Sacred Cross, or even Paladin Force at a wall) and the dash cancel with Free Air Dash fills the assist gauge through Assist Gauge Up Dash. On the other hand, its range and accuracy are limited (fixed diagonal movement, no tracking, 23F): keep it for punishing block staggers and slow whiffs rather than for poking.

The Paladin's main aerial HP attack for punishes and assist combos: a projectile which, if it connects, triggers an aerial combo with good homing finished by a ground wall rush. EX Mode: Job Augment! & EX Burst

The “Job Augment!” EX Mode: Regen, Critical Boost, Proteus and Inner Strength. EX Mode raises all his damage through criticals and Inner Strength (every attack at 1.5 times its power), and Proteus [R + Square] allows him to change job instantly without attacking, whenever Cecil is not in an attacking state (running, dashing, dodging), with no cooldown and repeatable in quick succession.

The major gain: no more need for telegraphed HP attacks to reach the other job, and Proteus is crucial in the Paladin Arts loop in combos — Cecil can thereby combo into Paladin Arts from Dark Knight while out of an attacking state. Careful, though: his stats (including run speed) still differ by job. The whole package rewards Paladin combos and EX Cores over the long term.

EX Burst : Face Shift: three simultaneous d-pad + button combinations to enter in about 3.5 seconds, read from left to right on both sides of the screen; a complete failure results in the weak “Darkness” finisher, which leaves Cecil as Dark Knight. Damage is average overall, fluctuating with the job changes and with the Dark Knight's passive ATK bonus.

Special moves

Special commands that never appear in the equip lists: they cost no CP and trigger from a dedicated input.

Proteus Special moveR + Square — EX Mode only

A special command available only in EX Mode: it allows him to change job freely, without going through an attack. Outside EX Mode, switching between Dark Knight and Paladin is only possible through specific moves — ground HP attacks or Dark Step towards Dark Knight, aerial HP attacks or Paladin Arts towards Paladin — which have to be equipped for the change to stay available.

Sources: dissidia.wiki/Cecil_Harvey_(Dissidia_012)

Unique mechanic

The job system: two jobs with radically different movesets — Dark Knight, geared towards ground combat, and Paladin, geared towards aerial combat. Each job has its own ground and aerial bravery attacks, while the HP attacks are shared. Only one job is active at a time, and the change happens through specific attacks: ground HP attacks or Dark Step (while Paladin) switch him to Dark Knight; aerial HP attacks or Paladin Arts (while Dark Knight) switch him to Paladin. Each of them has to be equipped for the change to be possible.

Cecil starts every fight as Dark Knight: reaching the Paladin's moves means committing to specific attacks — risky given how long his whiffs are, but unavoidable. In EX Mode, Proteus (R + Square) lifts that constraint by allowing a free job change without attacking.

  • Certain pieces of equipment modify his stats in a particular job: Cimmerian Edge (ATK +1 as Dark Knight) and Lightbringer (DEF +1 as Paladin).
  • Dissidia 012 adds two HP attacks: Shadow Bringer (Dark Knight) and Luminous Shard (Paladin), mutually exclusive — equipping one disables the other.
  • Competitively, Cecil generally specialises in a single job.

Gameplan & advanced tech

Play Cecil as a punisher: many of his moves have good vertical or lateral reach (Valiant Blow, Shadow Bringer and Sacred Cross to punish from various angles), and his reward comes from clean hits converted with an assist. As Dark Knight, hold the ground with your pokes (Shadow Bringer above all, a quasi-poke at 13F) and the Dark Flame anti-air; as Paladin, Radiant Wings serves as a quasi aerial poke, Sacred Cross as a vertical punish and Searchlight to occupy space at range.

Combos structure the gameplan: as Dark Knight, Dark Cannon opens into Valiant Blow or Shadow Bringer / Soul Eater, and assist conversions start from a wall rush or from the first part of Valiant Blow (Jecht is ideal for damage and for Dark Cannon setups by staying on the ground). As Paladin, Slash (cancelled into a Free Air Dash) leads into Radiant Wings for damage or Sacred Cross for EX, Searchlight > Paladin Force forms a solo HP combo, and the Aerith assist converts Sacred Cross into HP damage through a chase. Since his most reliable starters (Dark Cannon, Searchlight) are telegraphed low-priority projectiles, the assist is what makes the whole thing dependable.

Manage the risk of the job system: every job change outside EX Mode goes through a telegraphed attack, so choose your specialisation according to the stage and the matchup — bearing in mind that a single job cannot be relied on on large stages. Your slow frame data makes filling the assist gauge on whiff dangerous: Radiant Wings with lock off and Slash's dash cancel are your least exposed options. EX Mode (Proteus + Inner Strength) is the long-term reward that lifts the job constraint: capitalise on EX-generating Paladin combos and on EX Cores to reach it.

Character-specific tech

Hit glitch (Searchlight)

After a Searchlight that connects, the hit glitch activates for Radiant Wings and Paladin Force: Paladin Force then swoops onto the opponent from long distances with vastly superior tracking. Cecil is one of the few characters to exploit this glitch well, and it directly improves his Paladin game.

Slash dash cancel

Slash can be cancelled into a dash on hit — a rare property outside dash feints and EX Revenge. With Free Air Dash, that links into Radiant Wings or Sacred Cross and fills the assist gauge through Assist Gauge Up Dash.

Lock off Radiant Wings

Used with lock off, Radiant Wings goes in the direction Cecil is facing: a way to build assist gauge a little more safely, since the opponent can no longer dash into Cecil and block as easily.

Sacred Cross as a dodge-counter (pseudo double dodge)

According to Hollowed's Competitive Cecil Guide (2011), a well-timed Sacred Cross passes under single-hit attacks (Hopstep, Rough Divide) and counters immediately, dodges even assists, and in practice gives Cecil a Tidus-style double dodge against certain attacks. The guide also recommends using it as a feint / tech trap: presenting an opening (a block, a dodge or a Searchlight/Paladin Force) that Sacred Cross actually covers, and countering the opponent who bites. Set to neutral Circle (lock off), it always attacks downwards and becomes a safe way to counter quickly and build assist gauge.

Sources: web.archive.org/web/20120107184432/http://dissidiaforums.com

Gravity Ball link glitch

The Competitive Cecil Guide notes that Gravity Ball, normally unable to combo into HP damage without a setup, can get one through the link glitch — preferably cast from below the opponent, where the glitch goes through more easily. Risky, but it adds an HP conversion to a move otherwise confined to harassment; its curved trajectory also lets it hit behind blocks from above or below.

Sources: web.archive.org/web/20120107184432/http://dissidiaforums.com

Documented solo combo routes

Searchlight and Paladin Arts are cited among the most versatile combo tools in the game: Slash > a small dash or a wall > Radiant Wings, Sacred Cross or Paladin Force; Dark Cannon > any ground melee attack; Searchlight > dodge cancel > EX Switch > Paladin Arts; Searchlight > anything except itself or Luminous Shard.

Sources: pastebin.com/8FWDXjvJ

Empty chase into an assist gauge reset

Sacred Cross, at both of its angles, offers the empty chase into an assist gauge reset; Nightfall falls just short.

Sources: pastebin.com/dKSWgUQ6

Documented combos (original notation, dissidia.wiki)

Main article: Cecil (Combos)

Cecil has a couple solo combo starters with both jobs, which can lead to bravery and HP follow-ups alike. Most of his attacks can be used as follow-ups, so Cecil has rather flexible combo routing. Cecil's most reliable starters (Dark Cannon & Searchlight) are telegraphed low priority projectiles, so he may need assist to do these combos more consistently. With assists, Cecil can get damage from unfinished attacks and wall rushes as well.

Dark Knight can combo with either Dark Cannon or Paladin Arts. Dark Cannon leads to other Dark Knight melee attacks, while Paladin Arts leads to Paladin attacks. Cecil gets decent damage with Dark Cannon starters, but its low damage can vary due to how projectiles move. On average, Dark Cannon can deal four hits (3x3, 3 / 9 total).

Cecil's combos expand considerably with Slash and Searchlight. Slash provides a few good Paladin combos on the ground. Searchlight also supports both jobs (and in EX Mode), and Cecil can do more if the opponent is on the ground. With Searchlight, Cecil can also go for the hit glitch with Paladin Force as means to do HP damage in the neutral.

Dark Knight Cecil can convert off of wall rush or with first part of Valiant Blow. Jecht assist is good for damage and Dark Cannon setups, and Cecil can stay on ground.

Main article: Cecil Combos (Aerith Assist)

Paladin Cecil uses wall rush and chase to set up HP damage with Aerith assist. If Cecil gets a ground wall rush, he can go for Slash combos to get even more bravery with Searchlight routes or EX with Sacred Cross.

Universal techniques (blodge, dash feint, lock off, dodge punishment): see the Techniques & glitches page.

Matchups

Seen from the opponent's side, Cecil comes across as a dangerous opponent: tehdr4g0n's Golbez guide (GameFAQs, 2012) describes two toolsets he switches between, and details what ground zoners fear — Dark Cannon eats their magic pokes with more range (a trade leaves both players at close quarters, where Cecil's options are the faster ones) and Nightfall combines a very fast fall with a stagger on block, which opens a Soul Eater or whatever else he wants. The documented counter-measures give the anti-Cecil plan in negative: dodge Dark Cannon instead of trading, anticipate Nightfall with an early dodge then punish with a jump. The Paladin is judged more threatening still: with Speed Boost++, almost as fast as Onion Knight, and Searchlight shuts down the opponent's zoning — a Searchlight that connects means a big guaranteed combo, to be avoided at all costs; his physical options, on the other hand, can be blocked and punished. It is up to Cecil to exploit that asymmetry: his projectiles are feared, his physical moves are not.

On Cecil's side, Hollowed's Competitive Cecil Guide (dissidiaforums, 2011) documents tools designed matchup by matchup: a well-timed Sacred Cross passes under single-hit attacks and counters — the named examples are Tidus's Hopstep and Squall's Rough Divide — to the point of giving Cecil the equivalent of a Tidus-style double dodge against certain attacks, assists included. Lightning Rise is to be kept as a counter in specific matchups: its magic block answers ground spells of the Thunder Barret type from Squall and protects against dodge punishes in Ranged Low. Against mages, Luminous Shard reflects Ranged Low attacks (the opponent then has to dodge their own spell on top of the blade) and Saint's Fall cuts through Cyclone, Flare, Windburst or Watera. So many one-off answers that make up, matchup by matchup, for his lack of a safe aerial poke.

The Firion view (b0untyhunter270's guide, GameFAQs, 2012) matches the risk/reward profile of the overview: Cecil's attacks are very easy to dodge — Dark Cannon, Valiant Blow and Shadow Lance can be seen coming and can be blocked or Shield Bashed, Radiant Wings and Sacred Cross can be dodged — but the one real alarm is Searchlight: if it connects and Cecil follows up with Paladin Force, he can hit you at any distance. Even opponents who dominate the neutral exchange therefore have to respect his projectile starters, and the EX Mode (Proteus + Inner Strength) that lifts the job constraint.

Sources: gamefaqs.gamespot.com/psp/605802-dissidia-012-duodecim-final · web.archive.org/web/20120107184432/http://dissidiaforums.com · gamefaqs.gamespot.com/psp/605802-dissidia-012-duodecim-final

Assist synergies

Cecil Harvey as an assist

Cecil is ranked Mid on the assist tier list (Muggshotter); the wiki provides no written evaluation of his role as an assist, only his data: Shadow Lance (ground BRV, 35F, Wall Rush, up to 50 base), Radiant Wings (air BRV, 19F, Wall Rush), Soul Eater (ground HP, 39F, Wall Rush) and Saint's Fall (air HP, 53F, Wall Rush).

Recommended assists

  • Jecht — For the Dark Knight: fast whiff punishes, conversions off the key moves and off the wall rush, solo combo setups, and a return to Dark Knight from Paladin on a hit within a combo.
  • Sephiroth — For the Dark Knight: whiff punishes and above all easy knockback cancels — with gauge available, Cecil no longer has to depend on wall rushes to convert into an assist.
  • Yuna — For both jobs: a Ranged Low priority that LV2 Assist Change does not stagger, conversions off the key moves and off the wall rush, effective within Cecil's range on small stages and close to the ground.
  • Aerith — For the Paladin: she converts Sacred Cross into HP damage by initiating a chase (with no EX depletion on hit), sets up solo combos anywhere and combos safely into Luminous Shard with no LV2 Assist Change stagger.
  • Tidus — For the Paladin: the fastest aerial whiff punisher, with less aerial combo potential but a ground assist that can wall rush for extended solo combos.

A community record of solo combo routes for all 31 characters, compiled by Eddiegames on the Discord DISSIDIA and published on pastebin (last updated December 2022). Cecil is described there with Searchlight and Paladin Arts as combo tools among the most versatile in the game.

Known limits

  • The wiki's Matchups page is a stub: the matchups section is sourced outside the wiki (tehdr4g0n's Golbez guide and b0untyhunter270's Firion guide for the opponent's view, Hollowed's Competitive Cecil Guide for the matchup-by-matchup tools); no matchup-by-matchup analysis from Cecil's point of view was found.
  • The documented bravery moveset is incomplete (only 6 moves detailed): Valiant Blow, Dark Cannon, Paladin Arts and Shadow Lance appear in the infobox, in the combos or in the assist data with no detailed move entry.
  • No written evaluation of Cecil as an assist: only the data table and the Mid meta ranking are available.
  • In the combo tables, the “Opponent Assist (Comrade's Vow)” values are marked “???” and some EX gains are partial.
  • The assist gauge gain per move is not filled in (empty columns).
  • The References section is empty: no attributable or dated community tech.
  • The community's empty chase record is undated (the solo combo record that accompanies it is dated December 2022): how current it is cannot be established.
  • The job of each bravery attack comes from the “Ground/Aerial (Dark Knight)” and “(Paladin)” sections of the 012 page on dissidia.wiki (which the automatic extraction had flattened into ground/air), and is confirmed by the “Dissidia 012” tables of the Cecil page on the Final Fantasy Wiki — which also list the two HP attacks specific to 012, Shadow Bringer and Luminous Shard. The HP attacks remain shared by both jobs.
